content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction profile for tinidazole with various drugs and substances. 1. Tinidazole increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine through an unknown mechanism. Patients should be monitored for calcineurin-inhibitor-associated toxicities, such as nephrotoxicity, cholestasis, and paresthesias. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Danazol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Didanosine and tinidazole together increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 17. Dihydroergotamine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 18. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of disulfiram by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. Alcoholic beverages and ethanol-containing preparations should be avoided during tinidazole therapy and for three days afterward to prevent adverse reactions such as abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing. Tinidazole should not be administered to patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks. 19. Docetaxel increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 20. Doxorubicin increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 21. Liposomal doxorubicin increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 22. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. Co-administration is contraindicated. Tinidazole should be discontinued at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution and should not be administered within seven days of completing dronabinol treatment. 23. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 24. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 26. Elagolix decreases the levels of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 27. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and contraindicated with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. 28. Encorafenib affects tinidazole metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4. Co-administration may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 29. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 30. Ergotamine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 31. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 32. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 33. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of ethanol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. Alcoholic beverages and ethanol-containing preparations should be avoided during tinidazole therapy and for three days afterward to prevent adverse reactions such as abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing. 34. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 38. Felodipine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 39. Fentanyl (including transmucosal formulations) increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 40. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 41. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 42. Tinidazole increases the levels or effects of fluorouracil by decreasing hepatic clearance. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, monitor for fluorouracil-associated toxicities. 43. Fluoxetine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 44. Fluvastatin increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 45. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 46. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 47. Fosaprepitant decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 48. Tinidazole increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Concurrent therapy requires monitoring for clinical response to tinidazole and signs of phenytoin toxicity (e.g., nystagmus, ataxia, dysarthria, lethargy). 49. Glyburide increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 50. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 51. Haloperidol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 52. Hydralazine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 53. Tinidazole and idecabtagene vicleucel together increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 54. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 55. Ifosfamide increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 56. Iloperidone increases the levels of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 57. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 61. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 62. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 63. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 64. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 65. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 66. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 67. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Caution is required, and close monitoring is recommended. 68. Lenvatinib increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 70. Lidocaine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used.
